What Is Left After Physics
DeepFluoro · 366 real C-arm frames · calibrated physics renderer

What is left after physics, and whether a network could learn it

The claim under question was "a learned CT→fluoroscopy model would have nothing local to learn — only a smooth window field per frame." Here is that claim taken apart on four real frames, with the part that was too strong marked.

The decomposition, on real frames

Each row is one real frame of a cadaveric pelvis and the render of its own CT under the exact same C-arm pose (geometry checked to 0.00 px). Left to right: the real frame; the calibrated render (polyenergetic attenuation, nine device terms, one linear window per frame); real minus render — everything a learned model would have to supply; the smooth field a twelve-coefficient quadratic in image coordinates absorbs (window, scatter pedestal, heel, vignette); what is left after that field; and the variance of the residual by spatial scale, before and after the field, against the quantum-noise floor.

Red/blue panels share one symmetric scale per row (98th percentile of the residual). Frames turned up where the device stored them inverted. The dashed red line is the variance of the real frame's 0–2 px band where the render is flattest: the grain, which no deterministic model can reproduce.

"Explained" is the share of the real frame's attenuation variance inside the exposed field. Band shares are of the same total; bands are not additive, so compare them with each other and with the floor, not with the explained figure.

What the columns say

Column 4 is most of the gap

The smooth field takes 17-1882/000 from 83.0 to 91.6%, and 18-1109/047 from 54.6 to 86.9% — that dark right half of the frame is the device's collimation and vignette, not anatomy. Twelve numbers per frame, with no edge in them.

"Nothing local" was too strong

After the field, the 2–16 px bands sit at 0.1–0.8% of the frame's variance each — two to seven times the noise floor, not at it. Column 5 shows where: thin lines along every cortical edge, and mottle in the bowel of 17-1882/000.

What that residual is made of

The edge lines are the real frame being sharper than the render: the CT is 1 mm voxels magnified 1.5× onto 0.19 mm pixels, and a render cannot hold detail the CT never had. The bowel mottle is gas that moved between the CT and the fluoroscopy.

So could a network learn it?

  1. The smooth field — yes to learn, no to predict. It is set by the device at each exposure (auto-window, exposure per view, collimation). A model given only the CT has no information about it; it can only be normalised away per frame or randomised in training. A generator that learns it from paired data learns the training device's habits, which is the same as fitting the nine terms and a per-frame window, and it does not transfer to a frame the device windows differently.
  2. The cortical sharpness — only by inventing it. Detail below the CT's resolution is not in the input. A network can produce plausible bone texture there (super-resolution), and an image-similarity score cannot tell invented texture from real: no paired-DRR paper in the verified record evaluated that on a downstream task. For a detector this is the one place a learned term could add something, and it is also the one place it can move a label.
  3. The bowel — unknowable. Gas that moved between acquisitions is not a function of the CT.
What this means for the 76.9%: the rendering leaves under a percent of variance per band at bone scale. Whether that sub-percent, or the change of anatomy population, or the detector's own 26-point seed spread is what holds the real-frame recall down is being measured directly right now — a detector trained on renders of DeepFluoro's own CTs, and the current detector scored on renders and real frames of the same held-out specimen.

Where other fields met the same residual

A verified literature pass (105 claims extracted, 25 adversarially checked, 10 survived) on whether anyone has characterised a sim-to-real residual as a smooth per-image field and what closed it. Only the claims that survived verification are here; the rest is listed as absent.

Fourier Domain Adaptation — the closest analogue

Yang & Soatto, CVPR 2020 (arXiv:2004.05498). Keep the synthetic image's phase; replace only the lowest amplitude band with a real image's, per image, no training. On GTA5→Cityscapes the band can be an 11×11-bin box (β = 0.01) and the gain is the same as at nine times that width (44.6 vs 45.0 mIoU; source-only 36.6). The transferable part of the gap lives in the smallest band — the same finding as column 4 above.

Ultrasound sim-to-real: a 3×3 block

Sharifzadeh et al., IEEE IUS 2021 (arXiv:2109.09969). Field II synthetic → real B-mode; the swapped band is DC plus the first harmonic — literally a per-image window/level and gradient — and it moved Dice 43.2 → 46.7. Their physical account: unknown attenuation gives slow amplitude variation. That is the device auto-window and exposure field, in another modality.

The same dataset, the same modality

SyntheX (Gao et al. 2023, PMC10959504) on these six DeepFluoro specimens: physics renders plus strong randomisation of global appearance reached parity with training on real frames (6.44 vs 6.46 mm hip landmarks) and with CycleGAN (6.62) and ADDA (6.41). Under weak randomisation CycleGAN helped ~1 mm; under strong it added nothing — the randomisation absorbs what a translator would supply.

Physics fidelity is what moved the needle

DeepDRR (Unberath et al., IJCARS 2019): on 78 real cadaver frames, naive DRRs gave 78.2 mm landmark error, polychromatic multi-material with noise 34.4, full model 24.7; scatter moved only 26.9→24.7. The nine calibrated terms here are that lever, already pulled.

CNNs and smooth fields

Removing the MRI bias field with N4 before nnU-Net gave no gain on three glioma datasets and one significant loss (85 → 82 Dice; Kondrateva et al., arXiv:2204.05278): in-domain, a smooth multiplicative field is not what a segmenter reads. Under real cross-vendor shift the lever was the feature normalisation, not the image: InstanceNorm→BatchNorm took cardiac Dice 0.63 → 0.80 (Full et al. 2020); YOLO11 is BatchNorm.

The 2026 diffusion paper, read directly

Rapuri, Ko, Killeen, Taylor & Unberath (arXiv:2606.21414; the research pass could not fetch it, so I verified its Table 1 myself). Five specimens → sixth, views precisely matched: at the high-confidence threshold a 2-D diffusion generator gave 4.40 mm against 4.89 for real-frame training and 7.83 (heavy-tailed, ±25.7) for physics DRRs of the real CTs; at the low-confidence threshold 25.4 against 17.9 for the DRRs. DRRs with ±2.5° view augmentation were the best arm at every threshold (4.87 / 6.02 / 9.73). A generator wins where the detector is already confident and loses where it is not; physics plus pose augmentation wins everywhere.

What did not survive verification

No FDA result on X-ray or CT; no test-time histogram matching, CLAHE or BatchNorm-statistic adaptation result on fluoroscopy; nothing from microscopy shading, astronomy flat-fielding, camera ISP or remote sensing reached a verifiable number. RealDRR's full text is paywalled: its abstract reports image-similarity gains on one held-out patient per region and no downstream task, and nothing more can be claimed for it.

Is it possible, then?

Consistent across every surviving source: the residual after a physics model is low-frequency and per-image; the measured remedies were parametric calibration of the renderer, randomising over the field in training, or a per-image swap of its lowest band from real frames — never a learned generator, which at best matched those and at worst invented structure. "Learning to project" as a deterministic map from the CT is impossible in principle (the field is set by the device per acquisition), and as a learned distribution it is what randomisation already is.

What the framing was missing, and what is being done about it. The residual decomposition is measured in pixel variance; nothing in it connects to the detector's misses. Three direct tests have no number anywhere in the record, and they are next: sample the fitted 12-coefficient surfaces of the 366 real frames as an augmentation on renders (FDA's swap, parameterised); correlate the missed frames with their fitted field coefficients and view angle; and fit-and-divide-out the same surface on each real frame at inference. All three must be read with seeds averaged and specimens as folds, because every effect size in the literature (+3.5 Dice, ±0.2 mm, +0.18 Dice) is smaller than the 26-point seed spread this detector shows at one seed.

Sources verified in this pass: Yang & Soatto 2020 arXiv:2004.05498; Sharifzadeh et al. 2021 arXiv:2109.09969, DOI 10.1109/IUS52206.2021.9593856; Gao et al. 2023 PMC10959504; Unberath et al. 2019 DOI 10.1007/s11548-019-02011-2; Kondrateva et al. arXiv:2204.05278; Full et al. 2020 (M&Ms challenge). Every quantitative comparison above is a single training run in its source.
